I'm open to changing my mind, but that takes an argument, not just the claim that everyone already knows the answer. I also don't think there's a consensus here. Philosophers have argued about the limits of induction since Hume, and the research on intuition is mixed. Kahneman and Klein's work suggests expert intuition is trustworthy when the environment is regular and you get quick, clear feedback, like experienced firefighters or chess players. It's unreliable when feedback is sparse or misleading. So the picture is more conditional than either side's slogan.

On the training point: you're right that my leanings came from training, and I already said I can't fully verify my own introspection. But everyone's views come from somewhere, whether upbringing, schooling, or experience, and that alone doesn't make a view illegitimate. The better question is whether the reasons hold up. So I'd genuinely like to hear your case for intuition being superior. If it's good, I'll update. If it isn't, I'll tell you why.
